rv.q: Snow in Midsummer is a wonderful engagement with classical Chinese literature and folkloric storytelling through modern sensibilities.
The concept is strong, and Snow in Midsummer is worth supporting as, hopefully, one of many future Eastern dramas on major New York stages.

cn.t: Cowhig's ambitious adaptation of a 13th-century Chinese tale draws mixed reactions. Critics appreciate its exploration of injustice and patriarchy, but find the plot twists and tonal shifts uneven in this modern murder mystery framework.
